key_facts: Multiple skin lesions on the lower legs
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography showed intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed dilated venous-like malformations with thrombosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, a history of intracranial hemorrhage, and the occurrence of multiple skin lesions with characteristics of vascular malformations support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome
rejected.why: While it involves vascular malformations, the syndrome typically presents with intestinal lesions and distinctive blue rubber bleb nevi, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves port-wine stains, varicose veins, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy, which are not the primary features described in the case.

rejected.label: Fabry Disease
rejected.why: Fabry disease is characterized by systemic involvement including pain in the extremities, gastrointestinal symptoms, and characteristic skin lesions (angiokeratomas), which do not match the presentation in the vignette.

rejected.label: Maffucci Syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is characterized by the presence of multiple enchondromas and vascular lesions, which are not the primary features of the case presented.
